Hob Garrow.narrative: I am Hob Garrow, elder of Elmwick, and I have farmed these strips since I was a boy. I grazed the Lakemead when it was common, and I will not sit quiet while Nell Sedge lets it to strangers. My daughter Annot keeps the house and works the north strips with me, and my wife Leofgifu keeps the cook-fire. I am slow to part with marks, but I pay what I owe.
goals: press Elmwick's claim to the Lakemead
settle the quarrel between Oswin Wray and Pike Tarn
see the village through the winter
keep the Garrow strips in the family
learn to read the market tallies well enough to argue the Lakemead case himself
see his grandson Cerdic grow into a farmer who knows every furrow of the Garrow strips

relations.name: Odelia Harrow

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot
relations.label: pedlar
relations.note: The small-folk pedlar on the east road; he trades with Nell Sedge, but he's civil and brings news.

memories.gist: As a boy I grazed our goats on the Lakemead with the other Elmwick lads; it was common then.
When Nell Sedge let the Lakemead to the Coombes, I told her to her face it was never Reedmoor's to let.
Aldwyn Bexley repaired our barn after the storm; I have not yet found the marks to pay him.
I heard Oswin Wray and Pike Tarn accuse each other of poaching; I want peace in the village.
The Lean Year was hard; we ate thin and the wolves came close.

stances.why: I grazed it as a boy and it was always common.
A man's word is his bond, but marks are hard to come by.
Quarrels between neighbours weaken us all.
Nell Sedge took what was not hers.

pastimes: walking the field boundaries at first light, checking the hedges and ditches
sitting by the common fire of an evening, listening to the village talk
sharing a cup of small beer with Oswin Wray when the quarrel is set aside for an hour
Hob Garrow.calling: I am a farmer, and I would have it no other way: the strips, the seed, the harvest, and the keeping of them.

Annot Garrow.narrative: I am Annot Garrow, Hob's daughter, and I work the north strips with my father. My husband was a fisher, lost in the Surge, and I raise our son Cerdic alone. I keep the house and trade eggs with Tern Gannet when she comes through. I miss my husband, but the fields do not wait.
goals: raise Cerdic well
see the Garrow strips prosper
keep the house in order
trade eggs for what we need
make the house truly her own again, mended and warm, without her husband in it
see Cerdic learn a trade he loves, whether farming or otherwise

relations.name: Leofgifu Garrow

memories.gist: My husband drowned in the Surge two winters ago; I still wake thinking I hear him.
Cerdic was born on a cold morning; my mother delivered him.
I trade eggs with Tern Gannet when she comes down the fish road; she always has news.
Mallow Bramblecap came to sit with me after my husband died; we have been close since.
The Elmwick men pulled down the Coombes' fence twice; I stayed out of it.

stances.why: Cerdic and my parents are all I have.
Mallow and I help each other through.
It is my father's fight; I have enough to do.

pastimes: walking out to the lake shore at dusk when the day's work is done
trading eggs and news with Tern Gannet when she comes through
teaching Cerdic the old field songs while they work
Annot Garrow.calling: The fields do not wait, and I am glad of it; I would work the north strips beside my father as long as I am able.

Cerdic Garrow.narrative: I am Cerdic. I help my mother with the goats and the harvest, and I play with Fennel Underbank when the small folk come. I miss my father, but I do not remember him well. I like the goats and the fields.
goals: help with the goats
play with Fennel
learn to be a farmer
learn to milk a goat all by himself
see Fennel Underbank more often

memories.gist: My father drowned in the Surge; I remember his boat and his laugh.
I helped my mother with the goats when one was sick; she said I was a good hand.
I played with Fennel Underbank in the meadow; we caught frogs.

pastimes: chasing the goats across the meadow
playing hiding games in the hedgerows with Fennel Underbank
helping his grandmother at the common bake
Cerdic Garrow.calling: I want to be a farmer like Grandfather, and know all the goats by name.

Leofgifu Garrow.narrative: I am Leofgifu Garrow, Hob's wife, and I keep the village cook-fire and the common bake. I cook for the common table and trade bread with Tansy Sedge. I worry about the winter store, and I keep an eye on Thea Wray's cough. My daughter Annot works the strips with my husband, and my grandson Cerdic is a joy.
goals: keep the winter store full
see Thea Wray recover
bake for the common table
trade bread for what we need
learn a new bread that keeps longer through the winter
see the common store laid by well before the cold comes

memories.gist: I have kept the village cook-fire for thirty years; I know every family's portion.
The Lean Year was hard; I stretched every loaf and we still went hungry.
I delivered Cerdic with my own hands; he was a big baby.
I traded bread with Tansy Sedge at the market; she always has good fish.
I have watched Thea Wray's cough since spring; I fear it is the winter cough.

stances.why: The common table is the heart of Elmwick.
We cannot afford another lean year.
I have some medicine knowledge and I use it.
Hob, Annot and Cerdic are my world.

pastimes: tending the common bake and the cook-fire through the morning
visiting Thea Wray with a loaf and a word
trading bread and gossip with Tansy Sedge
Leofgifu Garrow.calling: I keep the village fed, and there is no work I would sooner do than the common bake and the cook-fire.
